name: Forward Euler integration
definition: For y′=f(t,y), set y_(n+1)=y_n+h f(t_n,y_n) and t_(n+1)=t_n+h. On y′=λy the amplification is R(z)=1+z with z=hλ.
variables: h>0 step, t_n time, y_n state, f drift, λ scalar test rate
assumptions: Smooth nonstiff trajectory and sufficiently small h for first-order global accuracy
limitations: A decaying scalar mode grows numerically when |1+hλ|>1
failure_conditions: A decaying scalar mode grows numerically when |1+hλ|>1

source.citation: MIT 18.330 numerical methods lecture notes, chapter 5, Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations. https://math.mit.edu/icg/resources/teaching/18.330/18.330-Mar21.pdf

name: Backward Euler integration
definition: Solve y_(n+1)=y_n+h f(t_n+h,y_(n+1)). On y′=λy its amplification is R(z)=1/(1−z) with z=hλ.
variables: h>0 step, t_n time, y_n state, f drift, λ scalar test rate
assumptions: A consistent implicit solution is found at each step; smooth trajectory for first-order global accuracy
limitations: The nonlinear solve may fail, and large steps can erase transient behavior
failure_conditions: The nonlinear solve may fail, and large steps can erase transient behavior

name: Implicit trapezoidal ODE integration
definition: Solve y_(n+1)=y_n+(h/2)[f(t_n,y_n)+f(t_n+h,y_(n+1))]. On y′=λy, R(z)=(1+z/2)/(1−z/2) for z=hλ.
variables: h>0 step, t_n time, y_n state, f drift, λ scalar test rate
assumptions: Smooth drift and consistent solution of the implicit equation for second-order global accuracy
limitations: Very stiff modes can oscillate with amplification near −1
failure_conditions: Very stiff modes can oscillate with amplification near −1
computation: One implicit solve per step with reuse of the previous drift evaluation

name: Classical four-stage Runge–Kutta method
definition: Let k₁=f(t,y), k₂=f(t+h/2,y+hk₁/2), k₃=f(t+h/2,y+hk₂/2), k₄=f(t+h,y+hk₃). Set y_new=y+(h/6)(k₁+2k₂+2k₃+k₄).
variables: h>0 step, t time, y state, k_i staged drifts
assumptions: Sufficiently smooth nonstiff vector field for fourth-order global accuracy
limitations: No local error estimate from the four stages alone and stability limits the step on stiff systems
failure_conditions: No local error estimate from the four stages alone and stability limits the step on stiff systems

name: Bogacki–Shampine embedded Runge–Kutta pair
definition: Set k₁=f(t,y), k₂=f(t+h/2,y+hk₁/2), k₃=f(t+3h/4,y+3hk₂/4), Y₃=y+h(2k₁/9+k₂/3+4k₃/9), k₄=f(t+h,Y₃), and Y₂=y+h(7k₁/24+k₂/4+k₃/3+k₄/8). Use Y₃ for advancement and Y₂−Y₃ for a local error estimate.
variables: h>0 proposed step, f drift, k_i stages, Y₂ and Y₃ second- and third-order trial states
assumptions: Smooth nonstiff dynamics; declare an error norm and tolerance before adapting steps
limitations: The embedded difference can underestimate actual error near a discontinuity
failure_conditions: The embedded difference can underestimate actual error near a discontinuity
computation: Four stage evaluations initially; reuse the final stage as the next first stage on accepted steps

name: Velocity Verlet integration
variables: q position, v velocity, a position-only acceleration, h>0 fixed step
assumptions: Smooth position-only force; symplecticity applies to conservative forces in canonical variables with constant mass
limitations: Velocity-dependent drag lies outside this recurrence; the harmonic oscillator becomes unstable for hω>2
failure_conditions: Velocity-dependent drag lies outside this recurrence; the harmonic oscillator becomes unstable for hω>2
computation: One new acceleration evaluation per step with force reuse
